newsitem.title: USA: U.S. calls for release of remaining Peru hostages.
newsitem.headline: U.S. calls for release of remaining Peru hostages.

text.p: The United States on Monday called for the release of all remaining hostages held by Marxist guerrillas in Peru as U.S. officials said all seven American captives were now free.

A printed statement by White House press secretary Mike McCurry welcomed the release of the Americans who were among 225 hostages freed from the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima by Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels.
The State Department said seven Americans were among the group freed on Sunday night.
"That's everybody," an administration official said, meaning all the U.S. citizens were out. The guerrillas are still holding 140 people of various other nationalities.

"The president welcomes the safe release of the Americans who were held hostage in Lima and renews his call for the immediate release of all who continue to be held in the Japanese Ambassador's residence," McCurry's statement said.

"The United States expresses its great appreciation to the government of (Peruvian) President Alberto Fujimori for the support and consideration given to the Americans who were held, to their families, and to the entire American community in Peru," the statement said.
"The United States will continue its close consultations with Peru, Japan, and all concerned governments on this situation," the statement concluded.

The guerrillas said the Sunday night release of many of their hostages after five days of captivity was a goodwill Christmas gesture, but showed no signs on Monday of giving into Fujimori's demands that they lay down their arms and free the remaining captives.

Glyn Davies, acting State Department spokesman, said in a separate statement, "Our sense of relief on their release is tempered by the fact that over one hundred individuals continue to be held. We reiterate our call for the immediate release of all remaining hostages and our suppport for the Peruvian government's efforts to resolve this crisis peacefully."
